name: 177. Responses shell, apply_patch and allowed_callers vocabulary (PR #7292 / #7293 / #7301) (responses-tool-vocabulary)
description:
Three stacked Responses-API features, each wire-visible and each previously uncovered here.

PR #7292 adds the `shell` tool plus `shell_call` / `shell_call_output` message types. PR #7301 adds `apply_patch` and `apply_patch_call`. Both tool types were missing from the OpenAI `filterUnsupportedTools` allow-list, so they were dropped SILENTLY - the request still returned 200, just without the tool. A status assertion cannot see that, so every tool-acceptance case here asserts on `extra_fields.raw_request`, the bytes Bifrost actually sent.

PR #7293 translates `allowed_callers` between the two vocabularies. OpenAI calls the sandbox context `programmatic`; Anthropic names it by code execution version and rejects the OpenAI word, and OpenAI rejects Anthropic's versioned values just as flatly. Both directions are pinned. The collection already had `allowed_callers` coverage, but every existing row was Anthropic-native ingress sending Anthropic's own vocabulary - none crossed the vocabularies, which is the only thing PR #7293 does.

Two cases pin behaviour that is easy to get wrong in the safe-looking direction: a version-less `code_interpreter` must RAISE the emitted code execution version to 20260120 (20250825 has no programmatic tool calling, so an untranslated restriction would be unreachable), and an `mcp_toolset` must DROP the restriction rather than fail the request - Anthropic has no such field on a toolset, so there is no narrower state to fall from and erroring would only reject requests Anthropic would have served.

The streamed apply_patch case (177.12) pins the new stream fields: the apply_patch_call_operation_diff.delta events must reach the client and add up to the final diff, the .done event must keep its diff (a field BifrostResponsesStreamResponse did not have, so a re-marshal dropped it), and the closed item and response.completed must carry the full operation. 177.13 replays a function_call and an apply_patch_call whose outputs arrive patch-first: the patch output renders as user text and used to be written before the function tool_result, so the user turn after the tool_use opened with text and Anthropic rejected it; the tool_result must lead that turn.
